title: Objects as ball stoppers
question: In which of these situations does it count as intentional deflection of a golf ball in motion?

choices.text: A person kicks the golf ball on purpose
A club dropped by accident blocks the ball
Someone puts a water bottle in the ball's path to stop it
The wind blows the ball in another direction

explanation: Intentional actions, like kicking the ball or placing an object to stop it, count as intentional deflection. Accidents or natural influences like wind do not.
imagePrompt: A teenage golfer, right-handed, watches their golf ball on the fairway as it strikes a water bottle that was purposely set as a barrier.
imageAlt: A teen golfer watches their ball strike a water bottle purposefully placed to stop it.

issues: The golfer is depicted as right-handed rather than left-handed as specified in the scene requirements.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Adjust the golfer to appear left-handed, ensuring they are addressing the ball with a left-handed golf stance. The rest of the scene, equipment, and posture remain unchanged, with exactly one golf ball striking the water bottle.
